\subsection{Weights permutation}
\label{subsec:weights_permutation}
We recall that the permutation $\mathtt{p}\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda$ assigns to each weight $\lambda$ the bottom weight $\operatorname{bot}\L(\lambda)$ of the irreducible module $\L(\lambda)$; here $\lambda=\operatorname{top}\L(\lambda)$. In terms of the socle $\Ss(\lambda)$, this is the inverse of the map $\lambda^\vee=\operatorname{bot}\Ss(\lambda)\mapsto\operatorname{top}\Ss(\lambda)$; here $\lambda^\vee=\lambda\ot\beta$. Hence we can construct $\mathtt{p}$ using the characters $\operatorname{schar}(\lambda)$ computed in \S\ref{subsec:characters} via the following steps
\begin{enumerate}
  \renewcommand{\labelenumi}{(\arabic{enumi})}
  \item Given a weight $\lambda_i\in\Lambda$ find $\lambda_j=\lambda_i^\vee$.
  \item Compute $\lambda_k=\operatorname{top}\Ss(\lambda_i)$.
  \item $\mathtt{p}$ maps $k\mapsto j$.
\end{enumerate}
It also important to keep track of $\tau\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda$, namely $\lambda\mapsto\mathtt{p}(\lambda^\vee)$.

\begin{algorithm}[H]
\caption{Weights permutation $\mathtt{p}$ and $\tau$ from the socle characters}
\label{alg:weights_permutation}
\begin{algorithmic}[1]
\Require the characters $\operatorname{schar}(\lambda_1),\dots,\operatorname{schar}(\lambda_m)$ of the socles $\Ss(\lambda_i)$, stored as records (\texttt{data\_rec\_info}): for each degree $d$, the record of $\operatorname{schar}(\lambda_i)$ lists the pairs $(a,n)$ such that $\mathsf{M}_n$ appears with multiplicity $a$ in degree $d$;
         the permutation $i\mapsto j$ with $\lambda_j=\lambda_i^\vee$ (\texttt{lambda\_chek})
\Ensure the permutation $\mathtt{p}$ (\texttt{sigma}), the permutation $\tau\colon\lambda\mapsto\mathtt{p}(\lambda^\vee)$ (\texttt{tau}),
        and the indices $k_i$ with $\lambda_{k_i}=\operatorname{top}\Ss(\lambda_i)$ (\texttt{top\_of\_socle})

\State $\mathtt{perm\_list}\gets(1,2,\dots,m)$
\For{$i=1,\dots,m$}
  \State \textbf{(1)} $j\gets\lambda^\vee(i)$ \Comment{$\lambda_j=\lambda_i^\vee$}
  \State Let $d_\top$ and $d_\bot$ be the largest and the smallest degree of $\operatorname{schar}(\lambda_i)$
  \State \textbf{(2)} Let $T$ be the list of pairs of $\operatorname{schar}(\lambda_i)$ in degree $d_\top$
  \If{$T$ is not a single pair $(1,k)$}
    \State \textbf{error}: the top degree of $\operatorname{schar}(\lambda_i)$ does not contain a unique module
  \EndIf
  \State $k_i\gets k$ \Comment{$\lambda_k=\operatorname{top}\Ss(\lambda_i)$}
  \State Let $B$ be the list of pairs of $\operatorname{schar}(\lambda_i)$ in degree $d_\bot$
  \If{$B$ is not a single pair $(1,b)$}
    \State \textbf{error}: the bottom degree of $\operatorname{schar}(\lambda_i)$ does not contain a unique module
  \EndIf
  \If{$b\neq j$} \Comment{consistency check: $\operatorname{bot}\Ss(\lambda_i)=\lambda_i^\vee$}
    \State \textbf{error}: $\operatorname{bot}\Ss(\lambda_i)\neq\lambda_i^\vee$
  \EndIf
  \State \textbf{(3)} $\mathtt{perm\_list}[k]\gets j$ \Comment{$\mathtt{p}$ maps $k\mapsto j$}
\EndFor
\State $\mathtt{p}\gets$ the permutation $k\mapsto\mathtt{perm\_list}[k]$; \textbf{error} if $\mathtt{perm\_list}$ is not a permutation
\State $\tau\gets$ the permutation $i\mapsto\mathtt{p}(\lambda^\vee(i))$
\State \Return $\mathtt{p}$, $\tau$ and $(k_1,\dots,k_m)$
\end{algorithmic}
\end{algorithm}
